correctness.rationale: Acyclicity of chordal fan orientations and reversibility reduce exactly to triangle obstructions. Signed path runs give the rational transfer identity, recurrence, Fibonacci degree-n coefficient and maximum degree. An explicit signed-run conversion gives a degree-n-only path between every pair of simple orientations; the singleton run sandwiched between positive runs is handled by moving both source marks. Two separately structured programs test direct acyclicity and exact sign-run transfer, including simple connectedness in finite ranges.

originality.rationale: The 1993 fan orientation count, general chordal Hamiltonicity, Postnikov's zonotope correspondence and generic transitive-reduction criterion are prior work. The new degree generating function and connectedness of the induced simple stratum are not implied by these earlier results. Existing wheel and complete-split studies are different families or cover only excluded low-order cases. Residual risk of historical equivalent work is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Potential older equivalent enumerators under acyclotope, transitive-reduction or graph associahedron terminology, including unindexed or inaccessible texts.

value.rationale: This determines an entire infinite-family distribution of the natural local mobility of acyclic orientations, not just the known total count. The connectedness of the induced simple-vertex stratum, despite its exponentially shrinking fraction, is a nontrivial geometric property and a useful boundary for reconfiguration of simple zonotope vertices.
